texts: The salt-bloom new-moon harvest is a large collective ritual.
On the night of the new moon in salt-bloom season, a harvest party walks to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
The harvest party wears waxed coats.
The harvest party carries copper buckets.
The harvest party pours the salt-bloom into the Cauldron Hall salt-bloom store.

fields.sentence: The salt-bloom new-moon harvest is a large collective ritual.

q2_gaps: definite singular generic naming a recurring event kind ('The <compound> harvest is a large collective ritual'): the instruction set says a definite description picks out a specific thing and takes a witness, yet its own kind-level examples read a definite singular as the kind ('The dodo is extinct'), so nothing settles whether this is one occurrence (Member on a witness) or the kind (Inheritance on salt_bloom_new_moon_harvest)

a compound kind with two stacked noun premodifiers ('salt-bloom new-moon harvest'): the compound rules cover one modifier + head and coordinated premodifiers, but not how a three-part modifier stack is segmented
review.notes: Genus of the fused compound is emitted and the noun modifiers are correctly not exposed; 'large' and 'collective' are kept as separate descriptive atoms rather than fused, per the incidental-description bar.

fields.sentence: On the night of the new moon in salt-bloom season, a harvest party walks to the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.

q1_issues.issue: `new_moon` is decomposed as a compound kind (statements 1 and 2, asserting it is a subclass of `moon` and of `new`) yet is used nowhere as a kind — it appears only as a bare `Time` constant in statement 12 — so a time point is declared a class and the modifier genus is exposed on a non-compositional phase term.

q2_gaps: a time NP restricted by an of-phrase and a PP ("the night of the new moon in salt-bloom season") — Time atoms may compose across granularities, but there is no carrier for the restriction relation itself, so the composite time flattens into three independent Time values

a lunar-phase / invented-season time expression — the structured Time terms are only Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute, and the instruction set does not say whether a multi-word bare Time constant takes compound decomposition or stays opaque like a deictic

a multi-word proper name whose internal kind word is PLURAL ("the Salt-bloom Tide-pools") — the kind-word-inside-a-name rule is stated for a singular kind word ("the Kestrel River"), while the capitalized-plural-label rule bars taking a per-member kind from a plural label word, so the singular typing atom in statement 7 sits between the two rules
review.notes: The main clause is right: indefinite subject with a verbal predicate stays a witness (not a generic rule), the present tense correctly gets no status atom (no TODAY and no lexically-future adjunct), and the destination is Goal. The name atom preserves the surface hyphenation and emits no modifier genus on the name symbol, as required.

issues.reason: `new_moon` is used only as a bare `Time` filler, yet the two atoms place that same symbol on both sides of `Inheritance`, which 'requires a kind or property on both sides' — and the instruction set's own multi-word time constants (`this_morning`, `last_week`, `last_spring`) are emitted as opaque symbols with no genus and no modifier atom, so typing a time constant as a subclass of `moon` and of `new` is ill-typed content the words do not put there.

gaps_confirmed: A composite time NP restricted by an of-phrase and a PP ('the night of the new moon in salt-bloom season') has no carrier for the restriction relation, so it flattens into three independent `Time` values.

Lunar-phase and invented-season times have no structured `Time` term (the terms are only Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute), and no rule states that a multi-word bare `Time` constant stays opaque — the deictic examples demonstrate it but the doctrine never says it.

A multi-word proper name whose internal kind word is PLURAL ('the Salt-bloom Tide-pools') sits between the kind-word-inside-a-name rule (stated for a singular kind word, 'the Kestrel River') and the capitalized-plural-label rule (which bars taking a kind from a plural label word), so the singular typing atom is unresolved.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form keeps the lunar-phase time as an opaque bare constant — `(Time sk_walk_1 new_moon)` alone, with no `(Inheritance new_moon moon)` and no `(Inheritance new_moon new)` — exactly as `last_spring` / `this_morning` are emitted undecomposed.
adjudication.notes: The same collision sits unflagged on `(Inheritance salt_bloom_season season)`, the other decomposed `Time` constant. The rest of the clause is right: an indefinite subject with a verbal predicate stays a witness, the unanchored present correctly takes no tense atom, the destination is `Goal`, and the name symbol carries no modifier genus.

fields.sentence: The harvest party wears waxed coats.

q2_gaps: participial treatment adjective + noun ("waxed coats"): the fuse/split test puts material adjectives on the fusing side (wooden_bridge) while the instruction set's own participial-modifier example is split ("a laminated worktop" -> (Member sk_worktop_1 laminated)), and neither the term-of-art list nor the incidental-description list (colour, size, damage, mood) decides a treatment participle

a descriptive modifier on a NON-SPECIFIC bare-plural object: the bare-kind-filler route supplies no witness or group for the plural distributive rule to attach the modifier to, so fusing into a compound kind is the only expressible option
review.notes: Given the fusion, the atoms are internally consistent with Compound concepts: head genus (Inheritance waxed_coat coat) always emitted, modifier genus licensed by the predication test ("the coat is waxed"), and harvest suppressed as a noun modifier. The singular collective subject correctly takes a plain event with the group as filler, no distribution rule, and no status atom for the habitual.

fields.sentence: The harvest party carries copper buckets.

review.notes: The bare-plural object 'copper buckets' takes the bare kind filler rather than a group witness, which the episodic-vs-kind-level split licenses for this unmarked habitual present clause; 'copper' is correctly left unexposed as a noun modifier (the steel_beam line) and the singular collective subject correctly gets no distribution rule.

The event-denoting noun's own witness carries the extent, so 'lasts' is consumed by the interval End rather than reified as a separate last event -- the same treatment the instruction set gives 'lasted two days' as a duration measure on the eventuality. The bare present with no TODAY and no lexically future adjunct correctly gets no tense atom, and dawn is a licensed day-part constant in the term slot.

fields.sentence: The harvest party pours the salt-bloom into the Cauldron Hall salt-bloom store.

review.notes: The proper-noun premodifier is handled exactly per the 'Northgate spokesman' rule: the head phrase parses on its own with its compound genus and links to the named entity by opaque Possession, with no invented LocatedIn or PartOf. Motion-result 'pours ... into' correctly takes Theme + Goal with no Result atom; the witness symbol sk_saltbloom_1 elides the class underscore (sk_salt_bloom_1) but is still minted from the class.
